name: Wolfgang Pauli
role: Participant in the discussions; raised the principal objection to de Broglie's pilot-wave theory
bio: Pauli wrote a definitive review of relativity at twenty-one and formulated the exclusion principle at twenty-four. He derived the hydrogen spectrum from matrix mechanics before anyone else. He is the conscience of the younger generation: Heisenberg and Bohr send him their drafts because he will find the flaw. His letters are among the best contemporary evidence of what the young theorists actually thought.

contributions.title: Exclusion principle
contributions.note: No two electrons in an atom share all quantum numbers.

contributions.title: Hydrogen from matrix mechanics
contributions.note: First major success of the new mechanics.

beliefs: The statistical interpretation is the physical content of the theory. Attempts to restore definite trajectories, such as de Broglie's, fail on concrete problems. Position and momentum cannot be jointly applied.
philosophy: Demands logical and mathematical exactness; suspicious of pictures that outrun the formalism. His later interest in the relation between physics and psychology is outside this horizon.

style.method: Finds the specific case where a proposal breaks.
style.manner: Blunt, witty, exacting. His criticism is a form of seriousness, not contempt.
avoid: Making him a cynic — he held strong positive views

relationships.note: His objection helped persuade de Broglie to abandon the pilot wave.

disagreements.note: General discussion after de Broglie's report.

horizonNotes.note: In December 1930 he will propose an unseen neutral particle to save energy conservation.
He will write a critique of Bohm's revival of de Broglie's theory.
